candidates.name: Cerebellar Hemangioblastoma
support_spans: kinetic and static cerebellar syndrome with ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, bilateral nystagmus, and stage I bilateral papilledema
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a cerebellar lesion.

candidates.name: Medulloblastoma
support_spans: inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis measuring 40 × 31 × 29 mm
candidates.why: The location and appearance of the lesion are consistent with medulloblastoma.

candidates.name: Pilocytic Astrocytoma
support_spans: heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration
candidates.why: The imaging characteristics of the lesion are consistent with pilocytic astrocytoma.

candidates.name: Ependymoma
support_spans: lesion filled the foramen of Magendie, exerted mass effect on the medulla
candidates.why: The location and effects of the lesion are consistent with ependymoma.

candidates.name: Atypical Teratoid/Rhabdoid Tumor
support_spans: elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal on magnetic resonance spectroscopy
candidates.why: The spectroscopic findings are consistent with atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor.

candidates.name: Von Hippel-Lindau Disease
support_spans: cerebellar hemangioblastoma is a common manifestation of von Hippel-Lindau disease
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a diagnosis of von Hippel-Lindau disease.

candidates.name: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
support_spans: optic glioma and other brain tumors are common in neurofibromatosis type 1
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could be consistent with neurofibromatosis type 1.

candidates.name: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
support_spans: subependymal giant cell astrocytoma is a common manifestation of tuberous sclerosis complex
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could be consistent with tuberous sclerosis complex.

candidates.name: Li-Fraumeni Syndrome
support_spans: brain tumors are common in Li-Fraumeni syndrome
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could be consistent with Li-Fraumeni syndrome.

candidates.name: Cowden Syndrome
support_spans: cerebellar gangliocytoma is a rare manifestation of Cowden syndrome
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings could be consistent with Cowden syndrome.
